body.statement: Can the sharp deletion expansion show \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to\infty\) when \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\)?  The handle is an order-two one-wave expansion uniform over exact ties and unequal inclusion probabilities, followed by random-complement moment cancellation.
body.justification: First-order equivalence is too coarse to exclude pilots larger than the candidate square-root scale but still negligible relative to the experiment.
body.gap: The required positive order-two deletion coefficient is not supplied by the available finite-population central limit theorems.
body.consumer: It supplies the upper-interior coercivity premise in the conditional global theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: A positive sharp deletion term for \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).
obligation.obstruction: First-order Gaussian convergence leaves an uncontrolled remainder of smaller order than \(1/n\) but not necessarily smaller than \(m/n^2\); exact ties and unequal inclusions preclude a smooth finite-score Taylor argument.
obligation.attempted: Reduced the contrast to one-wave oracle gains and proved their common first-order limit; the required order-two cancellation remains the finite-boundary problem.
obligation.partial_result: The first-order result proves only \(nD_{n,m}(\beta)\to0\) when \(m/n\to0\).  The desired endpoint conclusion needs the stronger positive term \(A(\beta)m/n^2\), whose order-two lattice- and inclusion-uniform derivation remains open.
